top_story.headline: FEC sends 23 RFAIs in three days, including three to sitting House members, but none of the letters could be read
top_story.dek: No filing in this batch could be described beyond its filing record, so nothing in it can be called a finding.
paragraphs: Of the 32 new filings, 23 are requests for additional information (RFAIs), one is a Form 99 and eight are termination approvals. The FEC's PDFs for the RFAIs and the Form 99 could not be read, so what each letter asks is unknown. The filing records show the committee, the report in question and the date received, and little else.

Three RFAIs went to committees of sitting House members: Rep. Donald S. Beyer, Jr. (D-VA), Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) and Rep. Virginia Foxx (R-NC). All three concern October Quarterly 2026 reports. Several committees received two letters at once, including Dr. Annie Andrews for Senate, the South Carolina Democratic Senate challenger, and Catholic Engagement PAC.
The batch is dated close to Election Day, which is Tuesday, November 3. Nothing in the available material points to personal use, embezzlement or another red-flag issue.

sections.headline: Three House incumbents receive RFAIs on their October Quarterly reports
paragraphs: All three letters were received by the FEC on 10/28, and each is two pages long. The PDFs could not be read, so the questions asked are not known. No other sitting-lawmaker filings, including terminations, appeared in this batch.

items: FEC sends Rep. Donald S. Beyer, Jr. (D-VA) an RFAI on the October Quarterly 2026 report of Friends of Don Beyer. The two-page letter was received 10/28 and could not be read, so the questions are unknown. (RFAI)

FEC sends Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) an RFAI on the October Quarterly 2026 report of Mario Diaz-Balart for Congress. The two-page letter was received 10/28 and could not be read, so the questions are unknown. (RFAI)

FEC sends Rep. Virginia Foxx (R-NC) an RFAI on the October Quarterly 2026 report of Virginia Foxx for Congress. The two-page letter was received 10/28 and could not be read, so the questions are unknown. (RFAI)

sections.headline: Twenty RFAIs go to challengers, open-seat candidates and PACs, none of them readable
paragraphs: Seven are for candidate committees and 13 are for PACs and party committees. Most were received 10/28, and the two Jim Schwartzel for Congress letters were received 10/27. Because the PDFs could not be read, each item below is described from its filing record only, and the questions and response deadlines are unknown.

Five committees received two letters each: Dr. Annie Andrews for Senate, Jim Schwartzel for Congress, Sarah for Iowa, Make the Road Action Political Committee and Catholic Engagement PAC. Whether the letters in each pair overlap is unknown.

sections.headline: One non-termination Form 99, from an Indiana House challenger, concerns loan forgiveness
paragraphs: The only non-termination Form 99 in this batch is from Phil Goss for Congress. The five-page PDF could not be read, so what the committee told the FEC is unknown beyond the filing's label.

items: Phil Goss for Congress, the committee of Democratic House challenger Phil Goss in Indiana, files a Form 99 labeled Loan Forgiveness. The five-page filing was received 10/28. Its text could not be read, so the loan and amount involved are unknown. (Form 99)

footer.coverage_window: FEC FRQ (RFAI) and Form 99 filings received October 26 through October 29, 2026. 107 filings were in the window, 75 of them reported in earlier editions, leaving 32 new.
footer.sources: FEC filings API; FEC Schedule A/B itemized transactions.
footer.known_gaps: The PDFs for all 24 RFAIs and Form 99s listed above (every RFAI plus the Phil Goss for Congress Form 99) failed to download or extract with HTTP 404, so none of their text was read and each is described from its filing record only. The Schedule A query for voided and negative transactions of $10,000 or more timed out (HTTP 504), so the Voided & Negative Transactions section could not be checked and is omitted.
